summary.headline: Ceinsys Tech Q2 FY27 operating revenue ₹160 crore, EBITDA up 20% YoY to ₹43 crore at 26.8% margin; H1 revenue flat at ₹317 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue was ₹160 crore with EBITDA of ₹43 crore (26.8% margin) and net profit of ₹33 crore, up 27% YoY. H1 revenue was broadly flat at ₹317 crore, with H1 net profit up 11% to ₹64 crore. Geospatial engineering services grew 73% YoY in Q2 to ₹130 crore, while technology solutions slipped to ₹29 crore. Management guided to subdued growth in Q1–Q3 FY27 until government funds are released, with growth expected to show in Q4; it gave no numeric guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Up from ₹27 crore, 16% of turnover in Q2 FY26
New orders ~₹231 crore added since 1 Apr 2026

financial_highlights.value: ₹446 crore per CFO Q&A; ₹422 crore in H1 FY27 per analyst

segments.name: Geospatial engineering services
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹130 crore (+73% YoY); H1 ₹225 crore (+52% YoY). Management said geospatial grew faster than mobility in international operations.

segments.name: Technology solutions
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹29 crore, slightly down YoY, attributed to project phasing. Management aims for geospatial and technology solutions to contribute equally on a yearly basis.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Including mobility, international was about 7–8% of consolidated turnover last year; management expects it to reach double digits this year. US operations show sequential improvement; UAE subsidiary planned in Abu Dhabi.

segments.name: AI / Astra AI India JV
segments.commentary: JV with AI Fabric USA incorporated 3 Nov 2026 for sovereign AI applications; business plan still under due diligence. Management said AI efficiency gains contribute about ₹25–30 crore of turnover this year.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give numeric guidance per company policy; it aspires to 20–25% growth but expects subdued growth in Q1–Q3 FY27 until government funds release, with growth visible in Q4.
Working capital cycle (debtor days including UBR) targeted at 125–130 days by FY27 year-end versus 125 days last year on a ₹660 crore base; range cited 125–145 days.
Majority of UBR expected to clear by 31 March 2027; about ₹250 crore of the ₹446 crore UBR is linked to Maharashtra projects, with a Maharashtra GR expected after a December cabinet session.

Management expects a decent order book by Q4 FY27 plus funnel; ticket size for new long-tenure orders typically above ₹25 crore. Two L1 orders awaiting final award; one or two of three transport-related opportunities expected in December.
Transport (ITMS/ATMS/MLFF) opportunity estimated at ₹10,000–11,000 crore, including NHAI corridor tenders of about ₹4,500 crore.
Acquisition ticket size around USD 20 million; two opportunities under evaluation; management does not expect closure in FY27. UAE deal flow expected within FY27.
capex_capacity: Abu Dhabi (UAE) subsidiary approved by board; incorporation started by December 2026, business development team already in place.
Doubling AI development workflows and adding AI-led products; expanded employee base in line with project needs.
Strengthening capabilities in ITMS, ATMS, MLFF, satellite imagery analytics, 3D city modelling and digital twin; leadership team being strengthened for business development.
Cash deployed in fixed deposits earning above 7.5%; management said no acquisition will be rushed.
demand_pricing: Order book ~₹805 crore at 30 Sep 2026; new orders ~₹231 crore since 1 Apr 2026. Recent wins: ~₹24 crore international AI-based monitoring order (US), ~₹28 crore LoA from Rightwater Solutions India, ~₹10 crore MSRDC extension.
Non-government share of revenue rose to 27% in Q2 from 16% a year earlier; the company is targeting a larger run-rate business outside government customers.
Margin trend: management said margin has risen 1.5–2% sequentially each quarter over eight quarters, from about 17.4% eight quarters ago to 26%.
Competition in transport tenders: three to four consortiums, each combining software, hardware and system-integration partners.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UAE subsidiary opportunity and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Target sectors are water and energy, with digital twin and 3D city solutions also in scope. Incorporation started by December; initial transactions are expected within FY27 and will be disclosed to exchanges once signed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company hit its growth target and what is the order pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is 20–25% growth, but H1 and likely Q3 will be subdued until government funds are released. Growth should show in Q4. Management would not give order-book numbers, only that a decent order book is expected by Q4 plus funnel.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins have improved 1.5–2% sequentially each quarter over the last eight quarters and expects further improvement from efficiency and AI-based delivery gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UBR and cash flow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: UBR rose to ₹422–446 crore. Management said about ₹250 crore is tied to Maharashtra JJM/IOT projects after a GR and cabinet approval, with UP payments of about ₹11 crore received and ₹14 crore expected. It said majority of UBR should clear by 31 March and that none of the amount is disputed.

qa_highlights.question: Why not a buyback given the low valuation and net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined: a ₹50 crore buyback would retire only about 7 lakh shares, and cash is needed for growth and acquisitions. It said the board would be informed of the suggestion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the two large L1 orders and transport opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Two orders are still awaiting final award. NHAI ITMS/ATMS tenders from February total about ₹4,500 crore. Management expects one or two of three opportunities to be awarded in December.

risks_watch: Unbilled revenue has risen sharply (₹67 crore in FY24 to ₹422 crore in H1 FY27) while operating cash flow was described by an analyst as negligible for three years; watch UBR conversion by 31 March 2027.
Dependence on Maharashtra and UP government funding; release of ~₹250 crore tied to Maharashtra GR is key.
H1 revenue flat and technology solutions revenue down; growth is expected to remain subdued in Q3.
Acquisition and AI JV plans lack disclosed targets, timelines or revenue projections; the AI JV business plan is pending.
Key management departure: a senior leader resigned, with the company saying no dispute.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, AI efficiency and the UBR recovery, but evasive on numerical guidance, order-book size, acquisition timelines and the buyback suggestion, which it rejected.
key_quotes: So I expect that the growth should be visible in quarter four.
We don't want to hush into any acquisition just for the sake of acquiring something.

adds.what: Abu Dhabi (UAE) subsidiary approved by board; incorporation started by December 2026

growth.why: Management gives no numeric guidance, only an aspirational 20-25% growth target, with subdued Q1-Q3 FY27 until government funds release and growth expected in Q4; backing is a ~₹805 crore order book and ~₹231 crore of new orders since 1 April, but no specific capacity additions were quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says margin rose 1.5–2% sequentially for eight straight quarters, from about 17.4% to 26%, and expects further gains from efficiency and AI-based delivery; Q2 EBITDA margin was 26.8%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Abu Dhabi subsidiary is board-approved with incorporation by December 2026 and a business development team in place, but no capacity or revenue figures were quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Target is 20–25% growth, but Q1–Q3 are subdued until government funds release and growth is expected in Q4, backed by an ~₹805 crore order book and ~₹231 crore of new orders since 1 April.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or utilisation figures were disclosed; cash sits in fixed deposits above 7.5% and management said no acquisition will be rushed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no numeric guidance and H1 revenue was flat at ₹317 crore, with Q3 expected to stay subdued.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1–Q3 growth is flagged as subdued and H1 revenue was flat, and conversion depends on ~₹250 crore of Maharashtra UBR clearing by 31 March 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is doubling AI-led workflows and adding AI-led products, but no named product launch or date was given; AI JV business plan is still under due diligence.

rows.label: Transport tenders (ITMS/ATMS/MLFF) award
rows.why: Two L1 orders await final award and management expects one or two of three transport opportunities in December; NHAI tenders total about ₹4,500 crore of a ₹10,000–11,000 crore opportunity.

rows.label: UBR conversion by 31 March 2027
rows.why: Unbilled revenue rose from ₹319 crore in FY26 to ₹422–446 crore, with majority expected to clear by March and ~₹250 crore tied to a Maharashtra GR after the December cabinet session; debtor days targeted at 125–130.

rows.label: UAE / Abu Dhabi deal flow
rows.why: Subsidiary is board-approved and incorporation starts by December 2026, with initial transactions expected within FY27 in water, energy, digital twin and 3D city solutions; international was 7–8% of turnover and is expected to reach double digits.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins (up 1.5–2% a quarter for eight quarters), AI efficiency and UBR recovery, but evasive on numeric guidance, order-book size, acquisition timing and the buyback, which it rejected; analysts pressed on cash conversion, UBR and the subdued H1.
